description_full: IQVIA Holdings Inc. provides clinical research services, commercial insights, and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries in the Americas, Europe, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. It operates through three segments: Technology & Analytics Solutions, Research & Development Solutions, and Contract Sales & Medical Solutions. The Technology & Analytics Solutions segment offers a range of cloud-based applications and associated implementation services; real world solutions that enable life sciences and provider customers to generate and disseminate evidence, which informs health care decision making and improves patients' outcomes; and strategic and implementation consulting services, such as advanced analytics and commercial processes outsourcing services. This segment also provides country level performance metrics related to sales of pharmaceutical products, prescribing trends, medical treatment, and promotional activity across various channels, including retail, hospital, and mail order; and measurement of sales or prescribing activity at the regional, zip code, and individual prescriber level. The Research & Development Solutions segment offers project management and clinical monitoring; clinical trial support; strategic planning and design services; and patient and site centric solutions, as well as central laboratory, genomic, bioanalytical, ADME, discovery, vaccine and biomarker laboratory services. The Contract Sales & Medical Solutions segment provides health care provider and patient engagement services, and scientific strategy and medical services. It serves pharmaceutical, biotechnology, device and diagnostic, and consumer health companies. The company has a strategic collaboration with Kexing Biopharm Co., Ltd. for biosimilar development. The company was formerly known as Quintiles IMS Holdings, Inc. and changed its name to IQVIA Holdings Inc. in November 2017. IQVIA Holdings Inc. is based in Durham, North Carolina.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 95K people. Revenue per employee of $172K ranks in the bottom quartile among Healthcare peers, improving at 10%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $22K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $3K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 42× revenue per employee (elevated relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (8/10).
financial_summary: IQVIA Holdings, Inc. is a large-cap healthcare business with a $44.8B market cap on $16.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $2.1B in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.95× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 3.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 23% over the past year excluding the latest month.

Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.8% (vs the 8% bar).

prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 8.8%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.24).
It converts 13% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.95x.
ROE of 21% is amplified by 4.6x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

hlth: Leverage is heavy at 4.1x net debt to EBITDA ($2.1B of cash against $15.7B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 3.0x.
The current ratio of 0.75 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 55% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 4.2% over 3 years, 7.5% over 5 years and 11.0% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 8.8% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.04, a backlog worth 2.1x annual revenue and deferred revenue up 19%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (3.7% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 19, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.1%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (9 sales, net $29.9M sold).
It returns 2.8% a year to shareholders (2.8% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 2.9% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 95,000 employees, each generates about $172K of revenue, 0.4x the Healthcare median, and productivity has risen 10.2% a year.
That works out to $22K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $7.2M (42x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
